script: I am tired of "future will be Mad‑Max." What's really ruining our optimism?. I am just done with this cult of pessimism that screams "future = Mad Max" if you're not on board. (I know, right?) The idiots in that club ignore every positive trend—literacy rising, medicine getting cheaper and better, crime dropping—and then they take the negatives and assume they'll just keep piling up. It's the same dumb logic that people living in the 1920s or the 2000s used, thinking wealth will just keep pouring in. (Literally insane.) They're basically playing a Pascal's wager of doom. If the world does go all dystopian, they're the wise prophet, basking in glory. If it doesn't, they're just "being careful." Optimists, on the other hand, get no glory when they're right—people just say they had lucky vibes. And when they're wrong, they're called "dumb sheeple" who fell into a disaster because they were too trusting. Pessimists don't actually predict anything. They're like broken clocks—right twice a day. When something bad happens they say "told you so." When nothing happens they say "it will happen." So their whole "prediction" is just "something bad will happen eventually." Which is the same as saying history isn't over and bad stuff will keep happening. (I mean, come on.) And there's a part of them that actually wants society to collapse. They're bored of their 9‑5, fantasizing about living in Fallout 4 and doing epic stuff. They're not just gloomy; they're literally craving chaos. And that, my friend, is the real tea.
